recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: US Secretary Of State Marco Rubio Meets Central Asian FMs In Samarkand, Holds High-Level Talks
recentItems.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio was in Uzbekistan on Monday to promote trade and ties with Central Asia, during a trip that came amid rumblings that America’s top diplomat is ignoring pressing matters in favor of politically safer visits and meetings.

The trip, which involves a stop in India later this week, seeks to promote U.S. economic and security ties with Central and South Asia.

In Samarkand, Rubio was meeting with his counterparts from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan under the C5+1 diplomatic forum, which brings together the five Central Asian countries and the United States to discuss security, trade and other shared concerns.

recentItems.title: Germany Falling Behind In AI? NVIDIA CEO Huang Urges Berlin To Catch Up In The Global AI Race
recentItems.description:
CEO of NVIDIA Jensen Huang on Wednesday urged Germany to take advantage of the computer industry and take the opportunities to thrive in artificial intelligence, ahead of his visit to Berlin.

Speaking to reporters at an event in the central London after the company announced a $250 million donation over five years to support U.K. agentic safety and security research, Huang said that with artificial intelligence everyone is at the "same place" and if Germany wants to use this opportunity, "this is the time to do it." "Nothing pains me more, frankly, than to see one of the most technologically advanced countries to be left so far behind in technology," said Huang, asked about Germany's role in the AI industry. Huang will attend the GTC Berlin this week, which runs from Oct. 20-22, 2026.
